title: Tidy the landing folder

ticket.subject: The landing folder is a mess and the loader keeps picking up the wrong files
body: The store exports land in `landing/`, and over the weeks it became a dumping ground: exports, photos from the
warehouse, half-finished uploads, a duplicate. Last night the loader read a partial file. Could you tidy it,
from the terminal (no file explorer), like this:
- the daily sales exports (`sales_<day>.csv`) go to `archive/sales/`, the stock exports (`stock_<day>.csv`) to
- `sales_2026-09-02 (copy).csv` is a truncated duplicate of the real export: delete it (keep the real one);
- every unfinished upload (`*.part`, wherever it is) is deleted, and so is the `landing/tmp` folder;
bash or PowerShell, as you like.

acceptance.text: The three daily sales exports are in archive/sales/, unchanged.

checks.fail: The export of 2 September is not the complete one.

acceptance.text: The two stock exports are in archive/stock/.
The rack photos are in photos/.
The duplicate, every unfinished upload (*.part) and the landing/tmp folder are deleted.

hints: `mkdir -p archive/sales archive/stock photos` creates the folders in one go (PowerShell: `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force archive/sales, archive/stock, photos`).
A glob picks the files: see what `ls landing/sales_*.csv` matches before you `mv landing/sales_*.csv archive/sales/` (PowerShell: `Move-Item`). Does it match the duplicate too?

A name with spaces and parentheses needs quotes: `rm "landing/sales_2026-09-02 (copy).csv"` (PowerShell: `Remove-Item -LiteralPath`). `rm -r` (PowerShell: `Remove-Item -Recurse`) deletes a folder and its content.
`find . -name '*.part'` (PowerShell: `Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.part`) finds the stragglers; is there one outside landing/tmp?
